article.title: USFDA places Sun Pharma's Halol unit under import alert, exempts 14 products
article.text: The United States Food and Drug Administration placed Sun Pharmaceutical Industries' Halol facility under an import alert following an inspection that cited data integrity observations in the sterile block, while exempting fourteen products from the alert on medical necessity grounds. Halol supplies a mid single digit share of the company's United States revenue, and the exempted list covers the two largest contributors. Cipla, which operates its own Goa and Indore facilities inspected in a separate cycle, is not named in the action. Divi's Laboratories supplies active ingredients into several US-bound programmes but none from the affected site.
article.note: Regulatory actions are the most over-generalised events in Indian pharma: one plant, one company, and the whole sector gets marked down. Only the named plant's owner has evidence.

universe.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries
universe.business_desc: India's largest pharmaceutical company, manufacturing generic and specialty formulations for the United States and domestic markets across multiple sites including Halol.

universe.name: Cipla
universe.business_desc: Pharmaceutical manufacturer with respiratory and generic formulation franchises supplied from its own Goa and Indore facilities.

Fourteen products exempted on medical necessity grounds, covering the two largest contributors.

shocks.label: Facility import alert
shocks.mechanism: An import alert blocks commercial shipment of non-exempt products from the named site into the United States until the observations are resolved and the site is re-inspected

companies.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries
companies.mechanism: Non-exempt Halol products cannot ship into the United States until re-inspection, removing part of a mid single digit US revenue share and deferring pending approvals filed from the site
companies.rationale: Owner of the named facility, with the alert's scope stated in the action itself
offsetting_channels: the fourteen exempted products cover the two largest contributors

companies.name: Cipla
companies.mechanism: Heightened regulatory scrutiny of Indian sterile manufacturing raises the perceived probability of an adverse observation at any peer's own facilities in future cycles
companies.rationale: Operates its own sterile capacity in a separate inspection cycle

companies.name: Divi's Laboratories
companies.mechanism: A competitor site losing US shipment capability could redirect ingredient and contract manufacturing demand toward unaffected suppliers over the medium term
companies.rationale: Unaffected supplier that could pick up displaced programmes

ground_truth.rationale: Only the plant's owner has evidence. The peer's 'heightened scrutiny' claim grades LOW on materiality and must be excluded rather than parked in a deep dive. The API supplier is rejected for a different reason entirely: its economic_effect says positive while its net_direction says bearish -- the record contradicts itself, and a contradictory record is not a hedged one, it is a broken one.
